summary: New idiom: mḏ̣ayaʕle/mḏ̣ayəʕ ruḥe ‘das Bewusstsein verlieren, ohnmächtig werden’

data.headword: mḏ̣ayaʕle/mḏ̣ayəʕ ruḥe ‘das Bewusstsein verlieren, ohnmächtig werden’
data.turoyo: Qayəm mədalli, naʕimo no, mḏayaʕli ruḥi bə ḥḏo naqqa.
data.translation: I got up and took it; I was a child, I lost consciousness at once.

rationale: Repeated reflexive loss with illness/pain and explicit absence of awareness at Jan 2.9/2118, 2.33/5438-5443. Exact and emphatic-spelling phrase searches found no duplicate. Jan 2.4/858 is supporting but its suffix segmentation remains open.

summary: New idiom: mḏ̣ayaʕle/mḏ̣ayəʕ hawne ‘den Verstand verlieren’

data.turoyo: Xəd ḥa d mḏayəʕ u hawnayḏe, mərle: Əno bəlḥuḏino? Əno bəlḥuḏino?
data.translation: Like someone who had lost his mind, he said, “Am I on my own? Am I on my own?”

rationale: Single comparison supports the mind-loss collocation without asserting an actual clinical state. No phrase hit in lookup; distinct from loss of consciousness with ruḥo.

summary: The 60 supplied occurrences were checked against full verses. Active human removal, accidental loss and annihilation all fit the existing II.1 gloss; no existing gloss text has been rewritten.

Repeated bare mḏ̣ayəʕ/mḏ̣ayʕo/mḏ̣ayʕi predicates occur after motion events and in reports of a missing state. The added Preterit filing is a reasoned proposal based on that distribution and the masculine/feminine/plural series, not a settled paradigm claim; unprefixed Infectum remains an alternative for some tokens.

Part. Pass. mḏ̣ayʕo no in PrS 65/39 is separated from bare finite candidates. First-person feminine mḏ̣ayʕono in PrS 44/59 may likewise involve a copular or finite analysis; the editors should compare both.
Final-ḥ forms and mzayʕo have not been silently emended or used to establish a box. Their analyses are rejected as secure evidence pending source checking.

Detransitive disappearance can conceal intentional removal: PrS 22/20 and 86/36 immediately supply relatives or jinn as agents in a separate taking clause. No agent is overt in the disappearance clause itself.
PrS 15/59, 22/19-20 and 45/8 overlap existing examples cited under older edition numbering; no duplicate additions or unsupported citation replacements.
Plain ḏ and emphatic ḏ̣ variants refer to this loss root in these contexts; no source spellings were normalized. Do not confuse the reveal root ḏyʕ.

miḏayaʕwole with lost item as subject and affected possessor -le supplies clear Detransitive Infectum-wa. In the government example the preceding clause names a remover, while miḏayaʕwo itself has no agent.

Past missing-record predicates mḏ̣ayaʕwo and copular mḏ̣ayʕo we/yo support a distinction between finite candidates and result descriptions; the unprefixed forms do not fully resolve round-1 paradigm questions.

Active Infectum-wa mḏ̣ayʕiwo has people as objects; do not infer Detransitive solely from a free disappeared translation. Bare mḏayʕənne at Jan 2.10/2530 is kept as the reader Preterit provisionally; suffix interpretation needs review.

ḏəyoʕo versus ḏəʕoyo is printed alternation in a lexical loss noun. Nomen Actionis filing records nominal evidence without inventing the regular Infinitiv. Part. Pass. -to in ṭaṣe mḏayaʕto is retained as a metaphorical lost-bowl description, not a new numbered city sense.

Confirm the Detransitive Preterit versus unprefixed Infectum and Part. Pass. distribution of mḏ̣ayəʕ/mḏ̣ayʕo/mḏ̣ayʕi, especially PrS 36/65-66, 44/59 and 65/39. Are any reduced forms active II with an intransitive use?
Verify final ḥ at PrS 18/45, 22/19, 29/25,29 and z in mzayʕo (PrS 49/52); no normalization has been made.
Is mḏ̣ayəʕ i səsto in PrS 74/40 active with the man as subject, or an agreement/text issue? The German makes the mare the subject; it was not selected.
Confirm the person/object segmentation in mḏ̣ayʕulle (JTM 1.6/2-3, PrS 86/7); the latter riddle was not used to establish a box.
Verify older PrS numbering before altering the inherited citations, including prs 128/35 versus supplied PrS 45/8.
Obtain checked editorial translations for every Jan quotation; all supplied English is machine translation.
Confirm the bare mḏayəʕ finite/result distinction and -wo in the missing-register predicates at Jan 2.4/476-477. First-round Preterit analyses remain provisional, not disproven by English tense.
Jan 2.4/707: confirm mḏ̣aʕye versus Mḏ̣ayʕe and whether dispersion is a conventional distinct meaning beyond this single paragraph.
Confirm suffix segmentation in mḏ̣ayaʕali ruḥi at Jan 2.4/858 and mḏayaʕʕe alay at 2.26/4379; source forms retained, neither used to infer a new paradigm.
Jan 2.35/5613,5664: is mḏayʕina a copular result predicate or active we squander with an omitted object? No independent spiritual-loss sense is proposed.
Jan 1.16/797: does hawi d mḏayəʕ have a losing owner or a lost-thing subject? Compare the clearer owner construction in /798; do not infer an active paradigm from this ambiguous token.
Is the lexical Nomen Actionis ḏəyoʕo/ḏəʕoyo a direct nominal borrowing, and what regular II Infinitiv do speakers use?
Time can be a resource that a person causes to be lost, while hawnayḏe is the subject of Detransitive loss of awareness. The grammatical frames differ despite related semantics.
Active elimination of people, time wastage, loss of awareness and threats all fit the inherited causative/loss gloss. ruḥo and hawno combinations are indexed as collocations.
Jan supports round-1 disappearance sense with missing people, records, books and language; spiritual loss is a figurative participant/domain extension, not another numbered sense.
